b2-15-01.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Boss Wanted
b2-15-01.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks why you are in a hurry after the meeting at the office. Your boss wanted everyone to hand in the report on Friday.
b2-15-01.prompt: Tell Meg what your boss wanted.
cues: Say what everyone had to hand in, and when
b2-15-01.target: Mi jefe quería que todos entregáramos el informe el viernes.
b2-15-01.english: My boss wanted all of us to hand in the report on Friday.
b2-15-01.canDo: I can form the imperfect subjunctive from the ellos form of the preterite.

b2-15-02.title: Communicative Challenge: The Same Tense
b2-15-02.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos finds si yo tuviese tiempo in an old book and asks whether it means the same as si yo tuviera tiempo.
b2-15-02.prompt: Tell Carlos whether the two forms mean the same, and which one you use.
cues: Say that the two forms mean the same
Say which one you use when you speak
b2-15-02.target: Sí, es lo mismo, pero yo siempre digo «si tuviera tiempo».
b2-15-02.english: Yes, it is the same, but I always say "si tuviera tiempo".
b2-15-02.canDo: I can tell that -ra and -se are two forms of the same tense with the same meaning.

b2-15-03.title: Communicative Challenge: At the Counter
b2-15-03.scenario: You are Meg. You are at the university office and you want to ask the clerk, politely, to explain how to do a procedure.
b2-15-03.prompt: Politely ask the clerk to explain the procedure to you.
cues: Say politely that you would like the clerk to explain how the procedure works
b2-15-03.target: Buenos días, quisiera que me explicara cómo se hace este trámite.
b2-15-03.english: Good morning, I would like you to explain to me how this procedure is done.
b2-15-03.canDo: I can soften a request with quisiera, pudiera and debiera.

b2-15-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Talks as If He Knew Everything
b2-15-04.scenario: You are Carlos. Meg asks about your new colleague at the office. He talks as if he knew everything, and you wish you knew more.
b2-15-04.prompt: Tell Meg how your colleague talks and what you wish.
cues: Say what you wish about yourself
b2-15-04.target: Mi compañero habla como si lo supiera todo. Ojalá yo supiera más.
b2-15-04.english: My colleague talks as if he knew everything. I wish I knew more.
b2-15-04.canDo: I can compare something to an unreal situation with como si + imperfect subjunctive.

b2-15-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Newspaper Means
b2-15-05.scenario: You are Meg. You are reading a newspaper article with Carlos. He asks what el libro que publicara en 1950 means.
b2-15-05.prompt: Tell Carlos what the phrase means and what kind of style it is.
cues: Say what the phrase means in everyday Spanish
Say what kind of style it is
b2-15-05.target: Es lo mismo que «el libro que publicó en 1950»; es un estilo formal.
b2-15-05.english: It is the same as "el libro que publicó en 1950"; it is a formal style.
b2-15-05.canDo: I can recognise a -ra form used like a past indicative, as in el que fuera presidente.

b2-15-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: The Class Reading
b2-15-consolidation.scenario: You are Meg. Carlos asks what your teacher wanted you to do for class. She wanted you to read a text about Gallegos and to talk about his novel.
b2-15-consolidation.prompt: Tell Carlos what the teacher wanted.
cues: Say what the teacher wanted you to read
Say what she wanted you to talk about
b2-15-consolidation.target: La profesora quería que leyéramos un texto sobre Gallegos y que habláramos de su novela.
b2-15-consolidation.english: The teacher wanted us to read a text about Gallegos and to talk about his novel.
b2-15-consolidation.canDo: I can form the imperfect subjunctive and use it after a past verb, with -ra or -se.
